sys_atf_test.name: Day-2 SAM: closure write-back is opt-in, works when enabled, and never blocks a real closure
sys_atf_test.description: x_fed_day2_ops.sam_closure_writeback defaults to false; when true, a SAM-originated task's closure attempts a structured write-back; when that write-back fails, the task still closes ok:true — SAM is the decision origin, not a dependency of ServiceNow's own closure.

sys_atf_step.description: Preconditions, plus SamCorrelationClient.writeClosureSummary's own contract in isolation: refuses with no sam_request_id, succeeds (canned) in test_mode, and honours the explicit ATF-only forced-failure hook.

Default is opt-in: with x_fed_day2_ops.sam_closure_writeback unset (or false), a SAM-originated task still closes normally — the property gate in MacdrOrchestrator.run() is read fresh on every run, so this needs no property mutation to prove.

Seed a SAM lineage row (clause 1 origin needs it), enable the property, and drive MacdrOrchestrator.run() end to end. Assert it closes AND that writeClosureSummary was reachable and succeeded for this request (checked directly, since the orchestrator does not surface the write-back result to its caller by design — see the "fail-open" note).

THE FAIL-OPEN PROOF: with the property enabled and the write-back forced to fail (request._forceWritebackFailure), the run must still close ok:true — a SAM-side failure at closure time must never turn a real ServiceNow closure into a stuck or failed request.
